answer: The cheapest real defence: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because gale only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, ocean is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any ember approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
